# Context
This fictional dataset contains information about patients stays at hospital including some demographic info and information about their reason for attendance. I will use this to create insights on healthcare trends in order to inform trusts about growing concerns around patient safety.

This data was sourced from Kaggle and uses the following tools: Python, Pandas, Matplotlib, Seaborn

```{python, data import, results = FALSE, include = FALSE}

import pandas as pd
import sklearn as sklearn
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

p4_data_import = pd.read_csv(r"C:\Users\Matthew.Webb12\Desktop\GitHub Repos\Portfolio3\python data\healthcare_dataset.csv")

p4_data_import.head()
p4_data_import.columns

# Creating count and percentage table to inspect columns
def variable_counts(column):
  counts = p4_data_import[column].value_counts()
  formatted_counts = counts.apply(lambda x: f"{x:,}")
  percentages = p4_data_import[column].value_counts(normalize=True).mul(100).round(1)
  result = pd.concat([formatted_counts, percentages], axis = 1, keys = ['count', 'percentage'])
  return result

condition_table = variable_counts("Medical Condition")
admission_type_table = variable_counts("Admission Type")
test_results_table = variable_counts("Test Results")
medication_table = variable_counts("Medication")
hospital_table = variable_counts("Hospital")

# I also want to create a matrix that counts the unique values in each column as it will make it easier to identify the most appropriate approach

unique_value_counts = p4_data_import.nunique()
unique_values_matrix = unique_value_counts.to_frame(name = "Unique Values Per Column")
print(unique_values_matrix)
```
This table of unique values is very useful as it indicates where the most appropriate analysis would be, I can't do any sort of hospital bench marking as there aren't enough rows per hospital.
